data.note:
Missed Protein degradation (ALLN) as Microtubule stabilizers.

What misled me: 10/100uM wells had taxol/docetaxel neighbours at 0.89 similarity with monotonic tub_mean rise and strong tub_glcm_contrast, plus multinucleation - I read this as stabilizer bundling + mitotic failure. A Protein degradation neighbour MG-132 was already in the pooled top-10 at 0.819 and 100uM alone at 0.844, but I discounted it. The per-well check showed the problem: 10uM margin was narrow (0.814 vs Eg5 0.801), 100uM top hit was cholesterol-lowering at 0.908, and the 3uM well was DNA damage/DNA replication-like at 0.90 - a pleiotropic stress profile, not a clean microtubule signature.

Literature supports the true biology: ALLN is a calpain/proteasome inhibitor; proteasome inhibition stabilizes regulators and triggers apoptosis/cell-cycle disruption, e.g. proteasome-dependent control of kinases and cyclins (PMID 12209081, PMID 15125768) and apoptosis induction by proteasome inhibitors including Bik accumulation and pro-caspase-3 sensitization (PMID 15824729, PMID 11319608). That explains multinucleation and textured tubulin/actin as downstream cytokinesis/mitotic failure rather than direct microtubule stabilization.

Lesson: weight MG-132-type neighbours and dose-discordance more; proteasome phenotypes can phenocopy stabilizers at high dose.

reflection.text:
The stabilizer call came from strong high-dose tubulin texture and intensity signals plus a pooled atlas match: tub_glcm_contrast z=+21.9 to +28.0 and tub_mean rho=+1.00 with 5/10 taxol/docetaxel neighbours. That evidence was real as a phenotypic description but secondary, and I over-calibrated to 0.82 despite the review-noted narrow margin and single-well dose-response with p=0.2.

What misled me was acquisition order and pooling: I sampled 10uM and 100uM first and ran compare_to_reference_atlas only on the pooled high-dose wells, so the discordant 3uM well with nuc_area z=+9.8 and nuc_major_axis z=+15.2 but no tubulin texture was not atlas-queried until requested. Per-well follow-up then showed 3uM as DNA damage 7/10 and 1uM as mixed epithelial/protein-synthesis-like, inconsistent with a direct stabilizer onset.

Unblinded as ALLN, a calpain/proteasome inhibitor, the multinucleation, low density, large misshapen nuclei and secondary tubulin bundling fit failed mitosis from blocked degradation, since proteasome control of cyclins and other regulators links directly to cell-cycle progression (PMID 15125768, PMID 26639105) and calpain plus ubiquitin-proteasome systems jointly mediate proteolysis (PMID 27880847, PMID 24691096). I never included protein degradation in the hypothesis set and did not test ubiquitin accumulation or comparator proteasome inhibitors.
what_was_right: Detected potent dose-related nuclear and cytoskeletal disruption with reduced density: nuc_solidity z=-23.7, tub_glcm_contrast z=+21.9 to +28.0, and microscopist multinucleation/low density
Measured monotonic tub_mean increase and rising frac_multinucleate_proxy with dose, correctly capturing failed mitosis/polyploid-like phenotype
After review, per-well atlases correctly exposed heterogeneity: 10/100uM stabilizer-like versus 3uM DNA-damage-like and 1uM mixed epithelial/protein-synthesis-like
what_was_wrong: Mistook secondary tubulin intensity/texture increase for direct microtubule stabilization rather than downstream consequence of proteasome/calpain blockade
Over-weighted pooled 10/100uM atlas 5/10 stabilizers and set 0.82 probability despite narrow margin over Eg5, visual Aurora/Eg5 call, and cholesterol-lowering neighbours
Acquired high doses first and ran atlas only pooled, delaying low-dose controls; relied on 4 single wells for dose_response with p=0.2 and ignored discordant 3uM large nuclei without tubulin change
Never hypothesized protein degradation and never searched for proteasome-inhibitor multinucleation mechanism until after unblinding

Inhibition of the proteasome stabilizes target proteins and changes cell state.
D-type cyclins are unstable proteins degraded by a proteasome-dependent mechanism.
Proteasome inhibitors cause accumulation of pro-apoptotic proteins and apoptosis induction.

## Conclusion

**Microtubule stabilizers** (stated probability 0.82); key evidence e5, e2, e3, e11, e4.

Why: Atlas 5/10 taxol/docetaxel at 0.89 similarity with dose-dependent tubulin increase supports stabilizer MoA.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Anti-tubulin immunofluorescence for bundled microtubules plus p-H3 mitotic index with washout to confirm stabilized microtubules vs Aurora phenotype.

## PI review

Verdict: request experiment.

Top MoA is plausible but 0.82 is over-calibrated: atlas margin is narrow (stabilizers 5/10, mean 0.874 vs Eg5 2/10, 0.842), 10µM phenotype favours Aurora/Eg5 with frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+7.4, and the tubulin jump rests on single wells with a discordant 3µM well (tub_glcm_contrast z=-0.25 despite nuc_area z=+9.8). Atlas was run only on the pooled 10/100µM wells, never on the later low-dose wells.

Requested: Free per-well compare_to_reference_atlas on the already-acquired 3µM well (dose index 4, rep 1, w_b9bba7558b): taxol/docetaxel neighbours before tubulin onset would support stabilizers; Eg5/Aurora neighbours would support the visual multinucleation mechanism and require lowering the probability.

## Unblinding

Compound: **ALLN** (PubChem CID [6915732](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/6915732))

Identity check: mismatch: name gives CID 6915732, BBBC021 structure gives CID 21118339 ((2S)-2-acetamido-4-methyl-N-[(2S)-4-methyl-1-oxo-1-(1-oxohexan-2-ylamino)pentan-2-yl]pentanamide)

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: agent said **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Protein degradation**.

## Reflection

The stabilizer call came from strong high-dose tubulin texture and intensity signals plus a pooled atlas match: tub_glcm_contrast z=+21.9 to +28.0 and tub_mean rho=+1.00 with 5/10 taxol/docetaxel neighbours. That evidence was real as a phenotypic description but secondary, and I over-calibrated to 0.82 despite the review-noted narrow margin and single-well dose-response with p=0.2.

What misled me was acquisition order and pooling: I sampled 10uM and 100uM first and ran compare_to_reference_atlas only on the pooled high-dose wells, so the discordant 3uM well with nuc_area z=+9.8 and nuc_major_axis z=+15.2 but no tubulin texture was not atlas-queried until requested. Per-well follow-up then showed 3uM as DNA damage 7/10 and 1uM as mixed epithelial/protein-synthesis-like, inconsistent with a direct stabilizer onset.

Unblinded as ALLN, a calpain/proteasome inhibitor, the multinucleation, low density, large misshapen nuclei and secondary tubulin bundling fit failed mitosis from blocked degradation, since proteasome control of cyclins and other regulators links directly to cell-cycle progression (PMID 15125768, PMID 26639105) and calpain plus ubiquitin-proteasome systems jointly mediate proteolysis (PMID 27880847, PMID 24691096). I never included protein degradation in the hypothesis set and did not test ubiquitin accumulation or comparator proteasome inhibitors.

What was right:
- Detected potent dose-related nuclear and cytoskeletal disruption with reduced density: nuc_solidity z=-23.7, tub_glcm_contrast z=+21.9 to +28.0, and microscopist multinucleation/low density
- Measured monotonic tub_mean increase and rising frac_multinucleate_proxy with dose, correctly capturing failed mitosis/polyploid-like phenotype
- After review, per-well atlases correctly exposed heterogeneity: 10/100uM stabilizer-like versus 3uM DNA-damage-like and 1uM mixed epithelial/protein-synthesis-like

What was wrong or missed:
- Mistook secondary tubulin intensity/texture increase for direct microtubule stabilization rather than downstream consequence of proteasome/calpain blockade
- Over-weighted pooled 10/100uM atlas 5/10 stabilizers and set 0.82 probability despite narrow margin over Eg5, visual Aurora/Eg5 call, and cholesterol-lowering neighbours
- Acquired high doses first and ran atlas only pooled, delaying low-dose controls; relied on 4 single wells for dose_response with p=0.2 and ignored discordant 3uM large nuclei without tubulin change
- Never hypothesized protein degradation and never searched for proteasome-inhibitor multinucleation mechanism until after unblinding

Proposed next experiment: Head-to-head ALLN versus MG132/bortezomib versus paclitaxel: proteasome chymotrypsin-like activity plus ubiquitin, p21, cyclin and securin western blots, with parallel anti-tubulin immunofluorescence, in vitro tubulin polymerization, and washout to test direct microtubule stabilization versus secondary mitotic failure from protein-degradation blockade.

## Citations

Citations verified: 5/5

- PMID [27880847](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27880847/): Activation of Both the Calpain and Ubiquitin-Proteasome Systems Contributes to Septic Cardiomyopathy through Dystrophin Loss/Disruption and mTOR Inhibition. *PLoS One* (2016) — Both calpain and ubiquitin-proteasome systems contribute to regulated proteolysis and protein turnover.
- PMID [26639105](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26639105/): E11/Podoplanin Protein Stabilization Through Inhibition of the Proteasome Promotes Osteocyte Differentiation in Murine in Vitro Models. *J Cell Physiol* (2016) — Inhibition of the proteasome stabilizes target proteins and changes cell state.
- PMID [15125768](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15125768/): Differential stability of Arabidopsis D-type cyclins: CYCD3;1 is a highly unstable protein degraded by a proteasome-dependent mechanism. *Plant J* (2004) — D-type cyclins are unstable proteins degraded by a proteasome-dependent mechanism.
- PMID [15824729](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15824729/): Bik/NBK accumulation correlates with apoptosis-induction by bortezomib (PS-341, Velcade) and other proteasome inhibitors. *Oncogene* (2005) — Proteasome inhibitors cause accumulation of pro-apoptotic proteins and apoptosis induction.
- PMID [24691096](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24691096/): Proteolysis of the human DNA polymerase delta smallest subunit p12 by μ-calpain in calcium-triggered apoptotic HeLa cells. *PLoS One* (2014) — Mu-calpain mediates proteolysis of cell-cycle and DNA-replication factors.
